stem: A team wants to check that a page stays usable when users enlarge its text. Which test best matches WCAG 2.2 Level AA expectations?

options.text: Zoom the browser to 200% and confirm the content and controls remain available and readable.
options.rationale: The resize-text requirement is about content and functionality surviving enlargement to 200%, not about a fixed font size.

options.text: Increase the monitor resolution and check that the text looks sharp.
options.rationale: A sharper display does not enlarge the text or test whether content survives enlargement.

options.text: Open the page in a narrow mobile viewport and check that it reflows.
options.rationale: Reflow at a narrow width is a separate concern; it does not show how the page behaves when a user zooms.

options.text: Confirm the stylesheet's base font size is at least 16 pixels.
options.rationale: A 16-pixel base is a design choice; users can still zoom, and the requirement is about the result at 200%.

explanation: WCAG 1.4.4 asks that text can be resized up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. The practical test is to zoom to 200% and check that everything remains readable and operable. A mobile viewport test covers reflow, and a fixed base font size does not guarantee the result under zoom.

references.title: W3C WAI — Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.4: Resize Text
